principle: The registry describes evidence sources and their capabilities. A registry entry never grants network access by itself; an implemented adapter is still required.

sources.name: Wikipedia
sources.role: Orientation and encyclopedic background for AION's existing curiosity questions.
sources.limitations: Not sufficient by itself for high-stakes, disputed, direct-human-perspective, or primary-source requirements.

sources.name: Official and primary sources
sources.role: Official documentation, public institutions, standards, and other primary evidence.
sources.limitations: A source-specific retrieval adapter is required before this capability becomes usable.

sources.name: Europe PMC open-access full papers
sources.role: Official EMBL-EBI literature discovery and full-text XML retrieval for open-access life-science papers.
sources.limitations: Life sciences only; full text is available only for the open-access subset and is bounded before synthesis.

sources.name: Audience and social signals
sources.limitations: Social signals are perspectives, not automatically factual evidence.

sources.name: YouTube public video metadata
sources.role: Discovery leads from public video title, description, channel, and URL metadata.
sources.limitations: Requires YOUTUBE_DATA_API_KEY. Metadata alone is not a human-perspective transcript and does not establish factual claims.

sources.name: arXiv open-access research abstracts
sources.role: Recent or specialised science and technology research evidence.
sources.limitations: Abstracts only. A preprint is not automatically peer-reviewed or settled fact.

sources.name: Hacker News public discussions
sources.role: Traceable individual public comments used as human-perspective evidence when a curiosity question explicitly requires perspectives from people.
sources.limitations: Hacker News users are not representative of humanity as a whole. Individual comments are perspectives, not factual authority, and must not be generalized beyond the evidence.
